tier_compliance.reason: The hint uses the samples' equal speeds and different masses to draw a comparative energy conclusion, rather than only connecting a visible detail to a science idea as tier 2 requires.

visual_grounding.reason: 'Both samples have the same average particle speed but different masses' refers to the displayed 1,000 m/s speeds and 46 u versus 26 u particle masses.

scientific_correctness.reason: 'The particles with the lower mass will have a higher kinetic energy per unit mass' is false: kinetic energy per unit mass is one-half speed squared, so equal speeds give equal kinetic energy per unit mass.

steers_toward_wrong_answer.reason: By attributing higher energy per unit mass to the lighter particles, the hint likely directs the student toward sample B, whereas sample A has the higher average kinetic energy and temperature.

answer_disclosure.reason: The claim favoring the lower-mass particles provides a strong clue toward sample B, although it does not explicitly name a temperature answer.

actionability.reason: It directs attention to the displayed speed and mass comparison, but supplies no concrete action and leaves the student to determine how to use that comparison.
